messages.content:
Seed molecule (SMILES): C#Cc1cccc(Nc2ncnc3cc(OCCOC)c(OCCOC)cc23)c1
No explicit objective; improve drug-likeness.
Propose 10 distinct single-point edits.

request.system: You are a medicinal chemist proposing structural edits. Return complete, valid SMILES for each edited molecule -- not fragments, not reaction arrows, not names. Keep the core recognisable: single-point modifications such as substituent changes, bioisosteric replacements, ring swaps or linker adjustments. Never claim an activity value; the edits will be scored by independent tools.

tools.name: propose_edits
tools.description: Propose medicinal-chemistry edits of a seed molecule as SMILES.

smiles.description: Full SMILES of the edited molecule.

edits.rationale: Replaced terminal alkyne (ethynyl) with nitrile; retains linear geometry and H-bond acceptor character of the quinazoline pharmacophore (erlotinib-like) while removing a reactive/less drug-like alkyne moiety, improving metabolic stability and synthetic tractability.

Swapped the ethynyl group for fluorine, a small bioisostere that reduces molecular weight and lipophilicity while retaining the electronic influence on the aniline ring, improving ligand efficiency and drug-likeness.

Removed one methyl from a methoxyethoxy side chain to give a free terminal hydroxyl, increasing polarity and hydrogen-bond donor count to improve aqueous solubility without altering the core scaffold.
Replaced one terminal methoxy with a primary amine, introducing a basic center to improve solubility at acidic pH and offer an additional vector for salt formation.
Shortened one methoxyethoxy chain to a simple methoxy group, reducing molecular weight and flexibility (lower rotatable bond count) to improve ligand efficiency.
Added a fluorine ortho to the alkyne on the aniline ring to block a potential metabolic soft spot and modestly increase metabolic stability while retaining similar steric bulk.
Introduced a methyl-branched hydroxyethyl ether in place of one methoxyethoxy chain, adding a stereocenter and H-bond donor for improved polarity while keeping similar chain length.
Extended one side chain with an additional ethylene glycol unit to increase polarity and solubility, testing the effect of greater PEG-like character on physicochemical properties.
Moved the alkyne substituent from meta to para position on the aniline ring, altering vector geometry to probe SAR while keeping identical atom count and functional groups.
Replaced the terminal methoxy of one side chain with a methylsulfonyl group, adding a polar, metabolically stable group to increase solubility and reduce lipophilicity.
